clue.text: A sneaker lining demonstrated extortion

indicators.note: a lining sits inside something, so these words are placed within the outer word

parts.note: demonstrated means showed, or shown
taken as written
Keds are a well-known American brand of canvas sneakers

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a shoe with a peculiar lining that turns out to be part of a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lining' reads like the inside of a shoe, which suits 'sneaker', but here it tells you to put one piece inside another. Keds are American canvas sneakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is American slang for extortion, getting money from someone by threats.

clue.text: Take off with explosive burst to cover performance

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece that covers another sits on top of it, so comes first
an explosive scatters things in all directions, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the word to be rearranged
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A rocket launches with a loud bang that drowns out the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests a launch, and 'explosive burst' backs that up, but the definition means remove an amount, as in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a number is to deduct it, which is what subtracting means in arithmetic.

clue.text: Judge hard-core fragment on speed

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another stands above it in the column
the core of a word is its middle, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of hard
a bit is a small fragment
rate means speed, as in a rate of travel

explanation.surface: A judge weighs a piece of hard-core evidence in a drug case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-core fragment on speed' sounds like drug slang, but hard-core is split: the core of the word hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee, the verb sense of judge.

clue.text: A very small quantity of Pine-Sol spilled

indicators.note: a spilled liquid ends up all over the place, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the brand name of a household cleaner, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked over a bottle of cleaner, leaving only a drop behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine-Sol is an American brand of pine-scented household cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians use the Greek letter epsilon for an arbitrarily small positive quantity.

clue.text: Shockingly, a host curses

indicators.note: something done shockingly is jolted out of its normal state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinner-party host scandalises the guests by swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths in the sense of profanities are curses, swear words uttered in anger.

clue.text: Animal's tail on back of crazed Athenian man

indicators.note: placed on the back means attached after the other piece
something crazed has lost its order, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word to be rearranged

indicators.note: a tail is the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of animal

explanation.surface: A deranged man of ancient Athens has an animal's tail stuck to his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal's tail' looks like a real tail on a creature, but it is just the last letter of the word animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel is a man's given name, so it can stand for a man in crosswords.

clue.text: Someone in a tub turns around and discards shirt — that's one way to get clean

definitions.text: that's one way to get clean

indicators.note: turning around makes the word face the other way, so it is read from the end
to discard is to throw away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: someone in a bathtub is a bather
T as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: A bather in the tub rolls over and pulls off a shirt to wash properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get clean' pretends to mean washing in the tub, but it means giving up drugs or drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is treatment by which an addict gets clean of drugs or alcohol.

clue.text: Seethed about our group's pollen generator

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: to seethe is to rage
we is the pronoun for our group

explanation.surface: A group of hay-fever sufferers fumes about the plant making them sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is': the wordplay is the pollen generator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a weed whose abundant airborne pollen is a major cause of hay fever in North America.

clue.text: Rich person claiming loss is cut by 50 percent

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the first word takes in the second

parts.note: the haves and have-nots: a have is a wealthy person
L stands for loss in sports records of wins and losses

explanation.surface: A wealthy taxpayer claims a loss and sees the bill cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Claiming loss' reads as a tax deduction, but claiming means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to reduce it to half, so a 50 percent cut halves it.

clue.text: Arsonist keeps toy soldier, moving head and tip of tongue with singer of the hit song whose elements can be found in the completed grid

definitions.text: singer of the hit song whose elements can be found in the completed grid

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the first word encloses the rest

parts.note: an arsonist burns things

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to a new place, rearranging the word

parts.note: G.I. Joe is the classic American toy soldier

indicators.note: the tip of something is its very end, here the front, so one opening letter is kept

parts.note: the tip of tongue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firebug holds on to a toy soldier, turning its head, and sings along.
explanation.walkthrough: BURNER keeps IGJOE plus T. Big Joe Turner first recorded Shake, Rattle and Roll in 1954; the grid holds SHAKEDOWN, RATTLESNAKE and ROLLTOP DESK.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Joe Turner was the blues shouter whose 1954 recording of Shake, Rattle and Roll was a rhythm-and-blues hit.

clue.text: Took care of college degree via high school examination

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
via means by way of
the SAT is the US college admissions test taken in high school

explanation.surface: Someone earned a degree by way of an exam taken back in high school.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after a child for its parents, so babysat means minded or watched over.

clue.text: Label a record in a foreign language

parts.note: a tag is a label
taken as written
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An archivist labels a record kept in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines, foreign from an American viewpoint.

clue.text: Twisting, neat stalker!

indicators.note: twisting the words bends them out of shape into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An admiring cry at a sinuous, tidy hunter slipping after its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a snake twists as it moves and stalks its prey neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a coiling venomous serpent that ambushes and hunts small animals.

clue.text: Ample commentary from someone who dislikes ambient music?

parts.note: Brian Eno pioneered ambient music
ugh is the noise of someone who dislikes something

explanation.surface: A music critic's sneer at background electronica is a generous serving of opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as the scornful remark 'Eno? Ugh!' from a listener who cannot stand ambient music.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough and ample both describe a quantity that is sufficient for what is needed.

clue.text: Killer environment for hot links

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A deadly setting for spicy sausages, perhaps an overheated grill.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot links are spicy sausages, which steer you toward food; 'links' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a series of connected metal rings, a set of links joined together.

clue.text: Extremely bright jewelry muffles noise

indicators.note: muffling wraps something up to deaden it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewelry
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A dazzling necklace somehow dampens the racket around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Light so intense it dazzles the eyes and stops you seeing is described as blinding.

clue.text: Lox holder beginning to feel "marvy"? That's retrograde nonsense

indicators.note: retrograde motion runs backwards, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: lox, smoked salmon, is classically served on a bagel

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of feel
marvy and fab are both dated slang for marvellous

explanation.surface: A deli customer gushes over a bagel in slang so dated it sounds like gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lox is smoked salmon, the classic New York bagel topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflegab is jargon-heavy, confusing talk, a slang word for pretentious nonsense.

clue.text: Neon light originally incorporates ridiculously clever unit that transmits signals

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into a body, so the outer pair goes around the rest
something ridiculous is absurdly out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ne is the chemical symbol for neon
the word to be rearranged

indicators.note: originally points to how the word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of light

explanation.surface: A clever little component inside a neon sign that passes on electrical signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Neon gives its chemical symbol, fitting a puzzle whose theme song mentions elements; 'originally' applies only to light.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell, or neuron, is the basic unit of the nervous system, carrying signals as electrical impulses.

clue.text: Ordinary restructuring of ward? Okay

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital administrator asks whether reorganizing a ward is acceptable, and gets a routine yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday describes the everyday and commonplace, the routine quality of a working day.

clue.text: Forgiving organized crime in anticipation of terrible flu

indicators.note: what comes in anticipation of something comes before it, fixing the order
to organize is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the first word to be rearranged

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: the second word to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lenient mob boss lets things slide while expecting a nasty bout of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organized crime' reads as the Mafia, but organized is only the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone merciful shows compassion and pardons offenders rather than punishing them.

clue.text: Discombobulated city ref: "Say, that one's crazy!"

indicators.note: discombobulated means confused and thrown into disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A flustered referee in a city game exclaims at a wild call or player.
explanation.walkthrough: To certify someone is to declare officially that they are insane, which is what the quoted remark does informally.
explanation.definitionFit: Certify has the sense of formally pronouncing a person mentally ill, the official way of calling them crazy.

clue.text: Failing old ship in Northern city

parts.note: F is the failing grade in US schools
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A sinking old vessel stranded in a city up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a description of the ship, but it is the school grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Fargo is the largest city in North Dakota, near the Canadian border in the US north.

clue.text: Dandy angle involving 25 very quietly

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in, so the first word encloses what follows

parts.note: to angle is to fish
25-across is a word for zero, written as the letter that looks like it
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: A well-dressed angler fishes in near silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 25-across is NOTHING, and nothing is the letter O. 'Dandy' could be the adjective meaning fine, but here it means like a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: Foppish describes a man overly concerned with fashionable clothes, as a dandy is.

clue.text: See 8
See 12
Stolen train is a place to stay

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
the el is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A hijacked train turns out to be a decent place to hole up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering rooms where travellers lodge for the night.

clue.text: Where to write and to spell "dork," possibly

indicators.note: possibly marks one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A school desk where a child learns how to spell an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To spell' looks like part of a spelling lesson, but all its letters join the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolltop desk is a writing desk with a sliding slatted cover, a piece of furniture for writing at.

clue.text: Unqualified to speak endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to talk is to speak

explanation.surface: Someone lacking credentials is barred from addressing the meeting at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' suggests lacking credentials, but it means absolute, as in unqualified success.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified as in complete, without reservation, is the same as total, as in a total disaster.

clue.text: Goose egg drink contains prune

indicators.note: something that contains holds another thing inside it

parts.note: nog is eggnog, the creamy holiday drink
to thin out a plant is to prune it

explanation.surface: An eggnog made with goose eggs and stewed prunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose egg' and 'drink' suggest eggnog, but goose egg is American slang for a zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose egg is a zero on a scoreboard, so it means a score of nothing.

clue.text: Mark leaves cab to advance in caboose

indicators.note: when a mark leaves, it goes away and is struck out of the word

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
an X is a mark made on paper
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A man named Mark climbs out of a cab to get ahead on a train's last car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A caboose is the last car of a freight train, and figuratively any tail end of a line.

clue.text: Race put down once again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a team race run in legs
second meaning: ..., to lay something a second time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down once again' sounds like a second insult or defeat, but it is laying something, such as a carpet, a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team running race, and to re-lay is to set down again, as with flooring or bricks.

clue.text: Disheartened boy gets sick alongside healthy singer of the hit song whose elements can be found in the completed grid

definitions.text: singer of the hit song whose elements can be found in the completed grid

indicators.note: to get is to take in, so the outer pair receives the following pieces
losing its heart means the central letter goes and the outside pair is kept

parts.note: the outer letters of boy, with its heart removed

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: ill means sick
hale means healthy

explanation.surface: A dejected boy falls sick despite being healthy, then sings a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: BY holds ILL and HALE. Bill Haley and His Comets had the big 1954 hit cover of Shake, Rattle and Roll; the grid holds SHAKEDOWN, RATTLESNAKE and ROLLTOP DESK.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Haley was the rock-and-roll bandleader whose 1954 version of Shake, Rattle and Roll became a hit.
